title: Cholera: protect your family
sources: WHO, Floods: how to protect your health: https://www.who.int/news-room/q-a-detail/how-do-i-protect-my-health-in-a-flood

scenes.heading: Cholera: protect your family
scenes.sub: Safe water · clean hands · quick ORS
scenes.narration: Floods can carry cholera into wells and water tanks. Cholera spreads through dirty water and food, and it can kill within hours. But it can be prevented, and it can be treated. Here is how to protect your family.

scenes.heading: How cholera spreads
steps: Floods carry it into water and food
scenes.narration: The cholera germ lives in the faeces of infected people. When floodwater or overflowing latrines reach wells, tanks and food, the germ gets in. Most people who swallow it have mild illness or none, but they can still spread it. Some become very sick, with sudden, watery diarrhoea and vomiting.

scenes.heading: 1. Make water safe
steps: Bring it to a rolling boil
Let it cool with the lid on
scenes.narration: First, make drinking water safe. Bring the water to a rolling boil, with big bubbles, then let it cool with the lid on. If you cannot boil it, use water treatment tablets exactly as the packet says. Use safe water for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth and making baby food.

scenes.heading: Keep it safe
steps: A clean container with a lid
Pour it out, or use the tap
Never dip hands or cups in
scenes.narration: Keep safe water in a clean container with a lid. Pour it out, or use a tap. Never dip your hands, or a dirty cup, into stored water.

scenes.heading: 2. Wash your hands with soap
times: Before eating or feeding a child
scenes.narration: Second, wash your hands with soap and clean water. Wet your hands and rub in soap. Scrub every part: palms, backs, between the fingers and under the nails. Rinse, and let them dry in the air. Do it after the toilet, after cleaning a child, before cooking, and before eating or feeding a child.

scenes.heading: 3. Keep faeces away from water
scenes.narration: Third, keep faeces away from water. Always use a latrine, never open ground, and keep latrines far from wells. Put children's faeces in the latrine too, and wash your hands afterwards.

scenes.heading: 4. Make food safe
steps: Cook it well, eat it hot
scenes.narration: Fourth, make food safe. Cook food well and eat it while it is hot. Wash fruit with safe water and peel it, and keep food covered.

scenes.heading: Watery diarrhoea? Act fast
steps: Mix it exactly as the packet says
Go to a health facility quickly
scenes.narration: If someone has watery diarrhoea, act fast. Start oral rehydration solution, O R S, straight away. Mix one packet with safe water exactly as the packet says, and give small sips often. Go to a health facility quickly, especially if the person is very weak, cannot drink, or is a young child. Most people recover with quick O R S.

scenes.heading: Safe water. Clean hands. Quick ORS.
scenes.vaccine: Oral cholera vaccine: take it where health workers offer it
scenes.narration: Where health workers offer the oral cholera vaccine, take it, and keep boiling water and washing hands. Safe water, clean hands, quick O R S. Share this with your family.
